result.title: FOE-Dreamer: Deployment-Efficient Learning of Cyber Defense Policies in Operational Networks
result.comment: 14 pages, 5 figures. To appear in the proceedings of the Annual Computer Security Applications Conference (ACSAC)
result.summary: Autonomous cyber defense is widely studied with deep reinforcement learning, but most work trains policies inside simulators because learning requires many trial-and-error interactions. Simulator-based training carries a fidelity gap: trained policies face authentication delays, partial action failures, service dependencies, and user traffic patterns that the simulator did not represent, and degrade on transfer. Training directly in the network being defended removes the gap but makes every interaction slow and costly, so sample efficiency becomes the binding constraint. Model-based reinforcement learning has reduced sample requirements on games and physical robots by orders of magnitude by planning inside a learned world model, but it has not been applied to defenders trained in operational networks. We present FOE-Dreamer (Factored Opponent-Enhanced Dreamer), a model-based reinforcement learning framework that trains a defender online and directly in a network on cloud infrastructure, without a simulator stage. FOE-Dreamer separates three sources of variation in the latent state: a controllable component driven by defender actions, an exogenous component driven by benign user activity, and an opponent embedding inferred from defender-observable signals alone. Separating the components reduces the variance in policy gradients during planning in imagination. Against two scripted attacker profiles with user activity emulated by the GHOSTS framework on an 8-host OpenStack testbed, FOE-Dreamer trains within a 3-day budget on a single GPU and achieves about 2$\times$ better episode loss than Rainbow and IQN baselines under matched compute. Both the factoring and the opponent model contribute to the gain, and the learned latents are consistent with the intended separation.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 FOE-Dreamer，一个直接在真实运营网络中在线训练防御策略的基于模型强化学习框架，把 latent 状态分解为防御者可控成分、良性用户活动驱动的外生成分和仅由可观测信号推断的对手嵌入，并在想象中规划以降低策略梯度方差。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「可控/外生/对手」的 latent 分解与想象内规划，可能为 LVR 中区分任务必要状态与视觉旁路干扰、以及 latent 状态更新与贡献分配提供可供核查的方法线索，但领域差异较大，需自行判断可迁移性。
